unit.title: Что реально возможно на Android, iOS и консолях

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Details the two real mobile routes -- python-for-android/Buildozer for Android and the experimental pygame-ios for iOS -- and restates that consoles have no community path.
python-for-android is the packaging infrastructure and Buildozer the higher-level driver over it. -- Confirmed -- accurate description of the kivy toolchain relationship.

python-for-android's main repository contains no accepted pygame-ce recipe; only open community PRs and hand-attached custom recipes exist. -- Confirmed -- the kivy/python-for-android recipes listing contains no pygame, pygame-ce or pygame_ce directory, and PR #2971 ('Pygame-ce on Android') remains open and unmerged.

pygame-ios is a community Xcode-template tool its own author describes as not production-ready, with App Store builds untested and only some pygame-ce versions supported. -- Confirmed almost word for word -- seekerluke/pygame-ios README: 'This library is not well tested, and shouldn't be considered production ready'; 'Most importantly, I haven't tested App Store builds yet'; 'Not all pygame-ce versions are supported'.
iOS requires macOS with Xcode and a paid Apple developer account. -- Confirmed -- Xcode is macOS-only and App Store distribution requires a paid account.

Both correctly cited as the fuller treatment of a question already answered in outline. | motivation=Correctly frames both routes as engineering work with real prerequisites rather than an export button, and quantifies the cost (SDK/NDK, long builds, large APKs). | sequence=Correct position as the last of the distribution sections, hardest route last. | practice=No notebook, correctly.

Coherence: Every factual claim in this section was checked against the primary repositories and all hold. Together with 20.13 this is the most rigorously sourced material in the chapter, and more accurate than most published Pygame guidance on the same question.
